correctness.rationale: Dual Lipschitz potential differences give N_t(X,Y,Z)=max(|X|/t,|Y|,|Z|+(|X|+|Y|)/2); this remains a metric for 0<t≤2. Independent sign isometries average any feasible quadratic comparison to diagonal without increasing distortion. Exact first-octant polytope corner maximization gives P; dual linear-function norms give Q=max(1/(t²a),1/b,1/(4a)+1/(4b)+1/c). For t≤1, Q-normalized minimization is attained at (a,b,c)=(t^-2,1,4/(3−t²)); for t≥1, P-normalized KKT conditions give ((3−t)/4,(t+1)/4,1). The resulting BM² branches (7−2t−t²)/(3−t²), 1+4/((t+1)(3−t)) match at t=1 and monotonicity shows the unique minimum there. Independently reconstructed polytope constraints and numerically optimized positive diagonal forms at 6 t values including both endpoints, agreement <5×10^-10; analytic proof covers continuum and all nondiagonal forms.
